ingestion.notes: The processing pipeline (MAESTRO) is cited rather than described, so the specific QC, batch, clustering and annotation methods are not named in this paper.

enhanced_abstract.tldr: TISCH2 is a web resource of 190 uniformly processed and annotated tumor scRNA-seq datasets (~6.3 million cells, 50 cancer types, human and mouse), now with cell–cell communication, transcription factor, survival and gene-correlation analyses.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A tumor microenvironment single-cell portal. Datasets are found by text-mining GEO and ArrayExpress, curated by hand with sample metadata, then all processed through the same MAESTRO workflow: QC, batch removal, clustering, differential expression, cell type annotation, malignant cell classification and gene set enrichment.

sections.heading: Scale
sections.body: ~6.3M cells from 190 datasets across 50 cancer types and 20 tissues (about triple the first TISCH). 40 datasets include treatment conditions such as immunotherapy, chemotherapy and targeted therapy; immunotherapy datasets get extra responder-vs-nonresponder comparisons.

sections.heading: New analyses
sections.body: Cell–cell communication per dataset with CellChat (significant ligand–receptor pairs between cell types); transcription factor enrichment per cluster with LISA; survival hazard ratios across 33 TCGA cancer types; and gene–gene correlation computed on mini-clusters of 30 similar cells to reduce dropout noise.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: SPI1 and STAT1 came out as top regulators of a monocyte/macrophage cluster in head and neck cancer, and that cluster was predicted to suppress CD8 T cells via CD80–CTLA4.

key_findings: Uniformly annotated tumor datasets make cross-study comparison of immune cell types possible
All matrices, annotations, DEGs and interaction results are downloadable
limitations: Cell type labels come from an automated pipeline; their accuracy isn't benchmarked in this paper
Methods details are deferred to MAESTRO and the first TISCH paper
enhanced_abstract.why_it_matters: Rule 3 (labeled tumor data resource, preferred). A large, cancer-specific source of annotated immune and tumor cells for benchmarking our agent in the setting the group cares about, including monocytes/macrophages and CD8 T cells. Its labels are automated, so they should be checked before being treated as ground truth.

sequencing.summary: Collects published tumor scRNA-seq datasets across platforms; platform recorded per dataset.

quantification.summary: Not described in this paper (handled by MAESTRO).

preprocessing.summary: Uniform QC and differential expression via the MAESTRO workflow; gene correlations on averaged mini-clusters of 30 cells.

batch_correction.summary: Batch effects between samples removed within MAESTRO; method not named here.

clustering.summary: Cell clustering within MAESTRO; method not named here.

annotation.summary: Uniform cell type annotation and malignant cell classification via MAESTRO, producing consistently labeled TME datasets.

cell_communication.summary: CellChat run per dataset with standard parameters; significant ligand–receptor pairs (p < 0.05) and communication probabilities shown per cell type.

algorithms.name: LISA
algorithms.description: Transcription factor enrichment from chromatin and ChIP-seq models.
